title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཝ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 99)
shelf_note: Madhyamaka commentary (subcommentary on a Madhyamaka syllogism against arising from self, with Sāṃkhya objection) in a Derge woodblock folio: belongs in the Derge Tengyur dbu ma section.

tr_errors_A.english: the horn of a rabbit eliminates the arising of the three worlds," they say
tr_errors_A.problem: the example clause is construed with the rabbit's horn as agent; the source is 'just as refuting the arising of the three worlds from a rabbit's horn' (A renders it correctly two paragraphs later)

tr_errors_A.english: "Arbitrarily" means according to one's own preconceptions.
tr_errors_A.problem: 'ངེས་སོ' left untranslated; 'preconceptions' slightly loaded for བསམ་པ

tr_errors_B.english: refers to the position previously refuted by the Madhyamaka
tr_errors_B.problem: སུན་དབྱུང་བའི is 'to be refuted'; B says the Mādhyamika already refuted it, confusing which statement was earlier (the statement, not the refutation)

tr_errors_B.english: Why? Because of this prior position to be refuted by the Madhyamaka regarding those who assert arising.
tr_errors_B.problem: the sentence runs on to the next folio ('among those who assert arising, [some ...]'); B closes it as a complete, garbled reason instead of marking the continuation
note calls a Sanskrit reconstruction the 'original'; the page is Tibetan

pages.prefer_reason: Both are faithful in the analysis of subject, probandum, reason and example; A's one slip (opening example clause) is corrected later on the page, while B misstates the opponent position as 'previously refuted' and closes the run-on final sentence wrongly.

book_verdict: Clean Derge folio with an accurate transcription as far as I can read it at this resolution; both English versions are serviceable with only moderate slips, A slightly better.
